title: Comparative Dynamics of Interest-Free Banking: Ethiopia and Global Market Perspectives
content: Purpose: This paper aims to analyze Ethiopia’s emerging interest-free banking sector in comparison with global markets, focusing on regulatory frameworks, product innovation, and financial inclusion. It seeks to identify opportunities and challenges for Ethiopia in adopting Sharia-compliant finance. Methodology: A comparative qualitative approach is employed, drawing on secondary data from Ethiopian banking regulations, case studies of Islamic finance in global markets, and international best practices. The study synthesizes insights from policy documents, industry reports, and scholarly literature. Findings: Ethiopia’s interest-free banking remains underdeveloped, constrained by limited legal harmonization, product diversification, and public awareness. In contrast, global markets particularly in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Europe demonstrate advanced integration of sukuk instruments, risk-sharing mechanisms, and cross-border financial innovation. Ethiopia shows strong potential for financial inclusion among underserved Muslim populations but requires significant institutional capacity-building. Implications: Policymakers should prioritize regulatory alignment, capacity development, and product innovation to enhance competitiveness. Banks must invest in awareness campaigns and partnerships to build trust and expand market reach. Lessons from global markets highlight the importance of governance standards and international collaboration. Originality/Value: This study contributes to the literature by situating Ethiopia’s interest-free banking within a global comparative framework. It offers actionable insights for regulators, practitioners, and scholars seeking to balance cultural authenticity with international integration in financial systems.
